rows.text: At its meeting on 25 June 2007, the Monetary Council considered the latest economic and financial developments and voted to reduce the central bank base rate by 25 basis points to 7.75%.
At its meeting on 25 June 2007, the Monetary Council considered the latest economic and financial developments and voted to reduce the central bank base rate by 25 basis points to 7.75%.
In the Council’s judgement, data for the past month provide evidence that inflation has passed its peak.

The seasonally adjusted month-on-month rate of core inflation – which is a good guide to underlying inflation – has fallen to 3%, a level consistent with price stability.
